summary: Zoo Vadis is a fast, cutthroat negotiation game where players openly bargain, bribe, and vote to move their animal up a shared hierarchy, with victory points doubling as the currency you spend to buy influence. It plays best as a social, table-talk-heavy experience where alliances shift constantly and the mechanics matter less than reading the room.
praised: Tight, clever design that layers negotiation, hidden VP tracking, and bribery into a short 20-40 minute package
Scales unusually well from 3 to 7 players thanks to the neutral, bribable peacock pieces filling out lower counts
High replayability driven by shifting alliances and table dynamics rather than the rules themselves
Polished Osprey Games production and quick teach for a negotiation-heavy title
criticised: Lives or dies on the group - a quiet, non-negotiating, or overly analytical table falls flat
Prone to kingmaking and runaway-leader dynamics common to open-negotiation designs
Feels derivative to fans of Knizia's other negotiation games (original Quo Vadis, Amun-Re, Medici, Ra)
Thin, pasted-on theme that's mostly an excuse for the voting/bribery structure

interaction.kind: trading and negotiation, open bribery and voting

win_criteria: Most points, one or two sources

scoring.why: Your final score comes almost entirely from laurels (victory points) you've hoarded and spent as bribery currency during voting, so the winner is whoever manages that single VP-as-resource economy best.
